answer: Latency Ledger Mechanism.** Each identity must keep a lantern lit by answering randomized, context-dependent prompts within a rolling window; unanswered prompts decay its score. New identities start at zero and only gain standing through long, uninterrupted response history, so an attacker must sustain genuine attention across every sock puppet for months. A copper deposit is forfeited on missed prompts, and a dune-shaped scoring curve makes early history count least, forcing parallel identities to multiply real labor time rather than capital.
